title: Resolve burst-window skew causing quota enforcement gaps across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers experienced intermittent outages over the last 72 hours due to a mismatch between burst-window evaluation and persistent quota state when requests are routed across multiple frontends and Dedicated edge nodes. The enforcement logic allowed transient over-bursting which exhausted downstream Dedicated GPU pools and triggered protective throttles, causing errors and request drops.

This ticket tracks the production bugfix, mitigation steps, and post-incident follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create an account with reserved quota and burst policy (e.g., base=100/min, burst=300/30s).
2) Send a traffic pattern of rapid spikes: 250 concurrent requests within a 10s window from multiple source IPs, routed through different frontends.
3) Observe quota checks pass on frontend A (stale burst tokens) while frontend B enforces a stricter view, causing downstream capacity exhaustion and 429/5xx cascades.
4) Reproduction is timing-sensitive; easiest to reproduce in staging with short TTLs for coordination caches and disabled prefix caching.
root_cause:
Race between local burst token caches and centralized quota ledger. Frontend instances maintain ephemeral burst counters with a default sync TTL of 15s. When routing sends spikes to different frontends, the local counters are not merged fast enough with the central Redis ledger used by Dedicated edge nodes, so the combined allowed burst exceeds actual capacity. Additionally, an optimization in the Private deployment path introduced a bug where the burst window was rounded down incorrectly (floor to seconds) causing asymmetric window boundaries across services.

Two code-level contributors:
- Hosted/Frontend: optimistic token cache TTL too long (15s) and no strong consistency path for cross-instance spikes.
- Private/Dedicated: burst window rounding bug in quota-evaluator (off-by-one second when converting ms->s) causing intervals to slip and double-count tokens across adjacent windows.
mitigation:
Immediate mitigations applied: 
- Reduced token cache TTL from 15s -> 2s on all Hosted frontends (config rollout completed 2026-03-03 04:20 UTC).
- Enabled conservative throttling fallback on Dedicated edge nodes when ledger sync lag > 50ms (hotfix deployed 2026-03-03 05:10 UTC).
- Manually scaled impacted Dedicated GPU pools for three affected customers and applied temporary request queuing to absorb the excess traffic.

These mitigations restored customer traffic within 90 minutes for most customers. Ongoing: deploying the code fix for deterministic burst window evaluation and stronger cross-instance coordination.

2026-03-02 23:10 UTC - First customer report (enterprise A) of spike-related 429s.
2026-03-02 23:35 UTC - Multiple customers report similar symptoms.
2026-03-03 00:05 UTC - On-call triage identifies quota enforcement asymmetry; incident declared.
2026-03-03 02:15 UTC - Investigated logs; found differing burst counters and synchronization gaps.
2026-03-03 04:20 UTC - Token cache TTL reduced globally.
2026-03-03 05:10 UTC - Conservative fallback enabled on Dedicated nodes; capacity scaled.
2026-03-04 11:00 UTC - Patch for burst window rounding submitted (PR #1876).
2026-03-07 16:40 UTC - Patch merged; internal canary rollout started.
2026-03-10 09:30 UTC - Canary reached 20% traffic; no regressions observed.
action_items:
- (ENG) Merge and roll out deterministic burst window evaluator to all runtime tiers (assigned Diego) - Target: runtime-1.22.
- (ENG) Implement optional strong-consistency path for quota check on high-risk routes (design doc linked).
- (PM) Communicate incident summary and customer remediation to affected accounts (assigned Mei Chen).
- (SRE) Add Grafana alert for cross-instance burst token divergence > 10% for >30s.
- (Product) Re-evaluate default token cache TTL and surface trade-offs in Console (assigned Priya Rao).
- (Legal/Trust) Prepare incident notice and RCA for enterprise contracts if requested.
- (QA) Add end-to-end regression tests for multi-frontends burst scenarios in staging harness.
- (Infra) Add leader-election fallback for Dedicated edge quota leader if Redis latency spikes.

Each action item has been added to follow-up issues: ENG-8432, ENG-8440, PM-420.
notes:
Design trade-off: lowering cache TTL increases Redis QPS; long-term fix is a hybrid approach — deterministic windows + occasional strong-checks for traffic with high burst variance. Consider rate-limiter sharding by customer to reduce cross-instance coordination.

Customer follow-up: Ops to offer 2 weeks of credits to customers who hit errors due to this incident; SRE to validate quota recovery windows before closing customer-facing communications.
postmortem_plan: Draft RCA to be completed within 7 days and published to affected customers and internal execs. Include timeline, root cause, why mitigations worked, and concrete SLO/operational changes. Present at next All-Hands.
